clue.text: Arrest man with hawk's head, a bit of a nut

parts.note: to cop someone is slang for to arrest or nab them
Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is shown as a man with a falcon's head

explanation.surface: A police arrest of some bird-headed figure, oddly tied to a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'hawk's head' tempts you to take the letter H; instead the whole phrase describes the god Ra.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is the dried kernel of the coconut, so it is literally part of a nut.

clue.text: Grouse to jump about — one left to rest

parts.note: to caper is to leap or frolic about
ca is the abbreviation for circa, about
I is the Roman numeral one
to lie is to rest or recline

explanation.surface: Someone frisks about and then one person is left to take a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' reads as a verb meaning complain, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The capercaillie is the largest European species of grouse, a woodland game bird.

clue.text: Church with gold roof: outside is dull material

indicators.note: the dull word sits around the others, enclosing them on both sides

parts.note: plain means dull or unadorned

indicators.note: in a down answer the gold sits on top of the church, like a roof

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church with a gilded roof is surrounded by something drab.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is fine ceramic, a material used for crockery and ornaments.

clue.text: Components of bread provided in dry measure

indicators.note: the parts of the word are taken apart and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: The ingredients of a loaf are listed by a dry measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided in' is just a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ardeb is a measure of capacity for grain used in Egypt and the Middle East.

clue.text: What's odd in funny Haydn symphony

indicators.note: the odd word is placed inside the funny word

parts.note: droll means amusing in a dry way
rum is old-fashioned British slang for strange

explanation.surface: A question about what is peculiar in an amusing Haydn symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's' is only a link; 'odd' is the old British slang sense of strange, not uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's Symphony No 103 is nicknamed the Drumroll, after its opening timpani roll.

clue.text: Sleazy bar given classification "not ace fun"

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable drinking place

indicators.note: the ace letter is left out of the classification word

parts.note: a rating is a grading or classification
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A seedy bar is graded as no first-rate entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverting means amusing or entertaining, which is to say fun.

clue.text: Our duty is to protect the language

indicators.note: the words guard the answer inside them, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A patriotic call that our duty is to defend our language.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Fish in river: land some for cooking

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: A fish caught in a river, landing some for the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Red salmon is another name for the sockeye, a Pacific salmon species.

clue.text: Ring secured by reduced deposit

indicators.note: the ring is held inside the reduced word

parts.note: less means smaller or diminished
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A ring held as security for a smaller deposit payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' suggests money paid down, but it is a geological one.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is a fine wind-blown sediment, a geological deposit of loam.

clue.text: After dissection, I preserved dead mammal

indicators.note: cutting up the words means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A lab worker describes preserving a dead animal after cutting it open.
explanation.definitionFit: Père David's deer is a Chinese deer species named after a French missionary naturalist.

clue.text: Latent mercy's stirred for woman murdering her husband

indicators.note: stirring the letters mixes them into a new order

explanation.surface: Hidden pity is roused on behalf of a woman who killed her spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Clytemnestra killed her husband Agamemnon on his return from Troy.

clue.text: Male in the drink about to join vessel — do this again

indicators.note: the male letter goes inside the reversed drink
the drink word is turned round

parts.note: beer is the drink here
an ark is a boat, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: A man fallen into the sea is about to board a ship again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' looks like slang for the sea, but it is a pint; 'about' turns it round. 'this' in the definition refers back to joining the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-embark is to board a ship again, repeating the act of joining a vessel.

clue.text: Gift for boy lost in forest

definitions.meaning: an old word for a gift for good luck at a new start
the fairy-tale boy abandoned in the woods with his sister Gretel

explanation.surface: A present for a child who has wandered off in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansel means a good-luck gift, and is also the boy in the Grimm tale.

clue.text: A province with street harbouring cunning freedom fighter?

indicators.note: the province and street together give shelter to the cunning word

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, a UK province
arch means sly or knowing

explanation.surface: A province where a street hides some crafty rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: An anarchist wants freedom from all government, so is jokingly a fighter for liberty.

clue.text: Arrived with man, keeping quiet! Anxious to avoid the paparazzi?

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: the man's name holds the quiet word inside it

parts.note: Ray is a man's name
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone turned up with a man who kept silent, dodging photographers.
explanation.definitionFit: Camera-shy describes someone who dislikes being photographed, so avoids press photographers.

clue.text: One of the 16s briefly associated with old shah's form of belief

indicators.note: the president's first name is cut short to its familiar form

parts.note: 16 down gives the Roosevelt presidents, one of whom was Theodore
Sophy was an old title for the shah of Persia

explanation.surface: A president linked with an ancient Persian ruler's religion.
explanation.walkthrough: The '16s' are Roosevelts, from 16 down; Theodore shortens to THEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical religious philosophy, a system of belief about divine knowledge.

clue.text: Weary maiden rejected virtue

indicators.note: rejecting the pieces turns them back to front

parts.note: to tire is to grow weary
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A tired young woman turned away from goodness.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, a quality close in sense to virtue.

clue.text: Former president showing resolve to reform?

indicators.note: reforming the words makes them over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An ex-president shows determination to bring about reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D Roosevelt were both presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Flowering plant at home blocking chimney

indicators.note: the at-home word sits inside the chimney word, blocking it

parts.note: lum is the Scots word for chimney
in means at home

explanation.surface: A plant growing at home is stopping up the chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Linum is the genus of flax, a flowering plant with blue flowers.

clue.text: Place in theatre must be tidy — never churned over inside

indicators.note: the turned word goes within the tidy word

parts.note: to groom is to make neat and tidy

indicators.note: turned over means read backwards

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: A theatre space must be kept neat, never stirred up within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never' must be taken in its poetic contracted form before 'churned over' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: The green room is the backstage lounge where performers wait in a theatre.

clue.text: In the auditorium confine one after another

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: to intern is to confine or detain

explanation.surface: Locking people up in a theatre hall, one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: In turn means in succession, each following the previous one.

clue.text: Endless twisting putting out one part of body

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off
the one letter is put out of the twisting word

parts.note: torsion means twisting
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Constant twisting knocks one body part out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: TORSION loses I ('putting out one') to give TORSON, then 'Endless' drops its N.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, excluding head and limbs.

clue.text: Pioneers modified chemical used in rubber manufacture

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Early innovators adapted a chemical for making rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: Isoprene is a hydrocarbon that polymerises to form natural and synthetic rubber.

clue.text: Scottish explorer with a coat

parts.note: Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: A Scottish explorer equipped with a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket, a kind of coat.

clue.text: Woman given name in collection of stories

indicators.note: the name letter goes inside the collection word

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings

explanation.surface: A woman is named in an anthology of tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Tense? Things will never get better!

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense formed with have, as in I have walked
a claim that the current moment is already flawless

explanation.surface: Someone nervous is told nothing could improve on now.
explanation.definitionFit: The present perfect is a verb tense, and also literally says now is perfect.

clue.text: College Master in homosexual practice involving many partners

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a former type of British college

indicators.note: the master letter goes inside the homosexual word

parts.note: gay means homosexual
M is the abbreviation for Master, as in a degree

explanation.surface: A college master caught up in a same-sex affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygamy is the custom of having more than one spouse at a time.

clue.text: Holy word leader put out — such will be hollow

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a mantra is a sacred word or chant

explanation.surface: A sacred word loses its first letter, leaving something empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra are anatomical cavities, plural of antrum, so they are by nature hollow.
